messages:
jordan_acmecorp: Hey team — after upgrading our app to @redwood/sdk-node v0.25.0 this morning some chat endpoints started returning 404 and our embedding calls return 400. Saw a burst of retries and one duplicate charge. Repro steps below, happy to provide more logs.

jordan_acmecorp: Repro:
1) npm i @redwood/sdk-node@0.25.0
2) run server (Node 18)
3) call chat create:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'gpt-4o', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }], sessionId: 'abc' });
```
Response: 404 { error: 'route not found' }

alex_support: thanks — can you paste the full response headers and the exact SDK import line? also did you switch any config (baseUrl, apiVersion)?

jordan_acmecorp: import was: `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk-node');` baseUrl default, no apiVersion override. headers show `x-rw-sdk-version: 0.25.0`.

maya_support: quick hypothesis: v0.25 shipped a route-name change (chat.create -> chat.createStream internally) and some param casing changed (sessionId -> session_id) — if your backend routing is still expecting the old names the server returns 404/400. Also noticed the SDK now auto-retries on 502 by default which can cause double submits for non-idempotent calls.

jordan_acmecorp: ah — we do send sessionId camelCase in many places. That would explain the 400 on embed calls (server rejects unknown param). any hotfix?

maya_support: short-term: pin to 0.24.1 (npm i @redwood/sdk-node@0.24.1) and set retries to 0 in the client config:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: KEY, maxRetries: 0 });
```
Also send an Idempotency-Key header for create calls to avoid duplicate billing on retries:
```js
await client.chat.create({ /*...*/ }, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'invoice-1234' } });
```

alex_support: Can you attach the server-side response bodies for the 400s? if they include a `validation` array we can map the exact param names to pass to the API.

jordan_acmecorp: pasted one 400 body in full: "{ \"error\": \"invalid_params\", \"details\": [{\"field\":\"session_id\",\"reason\":\"required\"}] }" — so server expects snake_case.

maya_support: yep that matches. We'll file a compatibility ticket — @raj_eng can you check whether we can add a temporary routing shim/alias at the API gateway that accepts camelCase params and translates to snake_case, and also map legacy route names for the next 48–72h?

raj_eng: @maya_support @alex_support I can add a fast shim at the edge to accept both field names and alias the old route names to the new handlers. Need approval for a short config rollout window. Will monitor for perf impact. ETA 2–3 hours once approved.

alex_support: for tracking: I created support ticket RW-7832 and linked the customer logs. Jordan, please keep the app pinned to 0.24.1 and add the Idempotency-Key for now. We will notify you when the shim is live, then you can test against canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: edge-config/shim-allow-camelcase (owner: raj_eng) — scheduled in 15m to canary region.

jordan_acmecorp: thanks — pinning now and adding header. I'll test once you confirm the shim is live. Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:

maya_support: follow-ups: (1) we'll add a short note in the SDK CHANGELOG and migration guide warning about the param casing and route renames, (2) engineering to decide whether to keep aliases long-term, (3) we'll explore making the SDK emit snake_case payloads behind a compatibility flag to avoid future friction.

alex_support: closing loop here once shim is verified and customer confirms no further duplicates. Jordan, if anything else pops up DM me and we'll escalate.

jordan_acmecorp: confirmed — after shim deployed to canary the same request returned 200 on first try. Will run more integration tests tonight. Thanks all!
